skill.description: Generate still images with Google Nano Banana 2 through the RunComfy CLI. The skill documents prompt patterns, model options, output settings, web grounding, and routing guidance for image generation workflows.
skill.summary: Generate RunComfy-hosted Nano Banana 2 images with guided prompts and output settings.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: The skill is a Markdown guide that intentionally relies on the RunComfy CLI and RunComfy Model API. Confirmed risks are limited to explicit external command execution, global CLI installation guidance, authentication setup, and third-party network submission of prompts. Most static hits are Markdown formatting, schema field names, documentation links, or relative links with no prompt-injection evidence found.

remediation.issue: External CLI installation and execution are required for the workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to install RunComfy from the official source, review package provenance, and run commands only in trusted project contexts.

remediation.issue: Prompts and generation requests are sent to the RunComfy Model API.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users not to submit confidential prompts, private customer data, or regulated content unless their RunComfy account permits that use.

remediation.issue: RunComfy authentication may create local credential state.
remediation.suggestion: Document token storage expectations and recommend RUNCOMFY_TOKEN for ephemeral CI environments with normal secret-management controls.

content.value_statement: Image generation prompts often fail when model options and output settings are unclear. This skill gives structured RunComfy commands and prompting guidance for Google Nano Banana 2.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to call the RunComfy Nano Banana 2 text-to-image endpoint.
Documents supported aspect ratios, resolution tiers, output formats, and safety tolerance.
Provides batch generation examples for up to four images per request.
Explains seed reuse for reproducible image refinement.
Describes optional web-grounded generation for current events or real entities.
Gives routing guidance for Nano Banana 2 versus related image models.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI and a RunComfy account or token.
Sends prompts and generation requests to a third-party RunComfy service.
Supports still text-to-image generation only, not video or image editing.
Limits each request to four outputs and documented resolution tiers.

use_cases.title: Draft Social Thumbnails
use_cases.description: Create fast 0.5K or 1K image variations for posts, ads, and campaign concepts.

use_cases.title: Prepare Design Mockups
use_cases.description: Generate product cards, posters, and layout concepts with quoted in-image text.

use_cases.title: Prototype Current-Event Visuals
use_cases.description: Use web grounding when prompts reference recent events, public topics, or real entities.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Image Draft
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one default image.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a 1K square image with Nano Banana 2 for this concept: [describe the image]. Save the result to my project output folder.

prompt_templates.title: Batch Concept Variants
prompt_templates.scenario: Create several fast options for review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate four 9:16 draft variants at 0.5K for this social concept: [describe subject, setting, style, and mood].

prompt_templates.title: Seeded Final Export
prompt_templates.scenario: Refine a selected direction with stable composition.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Nano Banana 2 with seed [seed number], 16:9 aspect ratio, and 2K resolution. Refine this prompt while keeping the same composition: [prompt].

prompt_templates.title: Web-Grounded Visual
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt that needs current context.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a web-grounded image for this current topic: [topic]. Use a concise subject-first prompt, enable web search, and explain the output settings used.

output_examples.input: A marketer asks for four vertical launch images for a new wellness product.
output_examples.output: The skill proposes a subject-first prompt, selects 9:16 draft settings, and runs a four-image RunComfy generation.

output_examples.input: A designer asks for a product card with the headline Brewed Quietly.
output_examples.output: The skill quotes the exact headline, describes placement and style, and selects a suitable aspect ratio and resolution.

output_examples.input: An editor asks for an image tied to a recent public event.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends web grounding, notes the added cost and latency, and sends the prompt through the RunComfy endpoint.

best_practices: Start prompts with the main subject, then add environment, style, camera, and output details.
Quote exact visible text and specify its placement when generating posters, cards, or labels.
Use lower resolution for ideation, then reuse a seed and increase resolution for final output.
anti_patterns: Do not enable web search unless the prompt needs current facts or real-world context.
Do not submit confidential or regulated content unless RunComfy is approved for that data.
Do not ask for unsupported aspect ratios, unsupported resolution tiers, or more than four outputs.

faq.question: What does this skill generate?
faq.answer: It generates still images using Google Nano Banana 2 through the RunComfy text-to-image endpoint.

faq.question: Does it require an account?
faq.answer: Yes. You need the RunComfy CLI and either a RunComfy login session or a RUNCOMFY_TOKEN value.

faq.question: Can it edit existing images?
faq.answer: No. This skill covers text-to-image generation. The source notes a separate Nano Banana Edit skill for editing.

faq.question: How many images can it create per request?
faq.answer: The documented endpoint supports one to four images per request.

faq.question: When should I enable web search?
faq.answer: Enable it only when the prompt depends on recent events, real entities, or current public context.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
